title: Reconstruct Batch Normalization
summary: Derive mini-batch normalization, learn where scale and shift enter, and implement both the statistics and forward transform.

parts.title: Normalize each feature
parts.prompt: Which axes should a dense-layer batch normalization operation reduce, and why are features normalized independently?
parts.answer: For a batch shaped (N,D), statistics are computed over N for each feature D. Independent feature statistics preserve feature identity while standardizing its scale across examples.
hints: The result needs one mean and variance per feature.

parts.title: Restore representation power
parts.prompt: Why add learned gamma and beta after normalization?
parts.answer: Pure normalization forces every feature to zero mean and unit variance. Gamma and beta let the network recover any useful scale and offset, including the identity transform when appropriate.
hints: Can normalized activations represent a nonzero bias?

parts.title: Training versus inference
parts.prompt: Why can inference not use the current example as a mini-batch, and what replaces batch statistics?
parts.answer: Single examples produce noisy or degenerate statistics and make predictions depend on other examples. Inference uses running population estimates accumulated during training.
hints: Inference should be deterministic for one example.

parts.title: Compute batch statistics
parts.prompt: Return (mean, var): the per-feature mean and variance of a mini-batch, computed over the batch dimension (axis 0).

parts.title: Implement BatchNorm forward
parts.prompt: Normalize a dense mini-batch and apply learned gamma and beta.
